previousFix.description: Root cause: ExerciseWheelPicker.handleLogSet declared the final set on set_number===targetSets, firing onSetComplete(true) even when earlier sets were unlogged (premature completion on top-set-first); and Activity.handleSetComplete re-fired the celebration when editing an already-logged final set. Fix: completion now gates on distinct coverage of ALL target sets 1..targetSets (ExerciseWheelPicker.tsx:350-353) and activeSet advances to the first still-pending set; handleSetComplete returns early when showWorkoutCompleteRef is already true (Activity.tsx:703) so editing the final set no longer replays confetti/sound. Verified: ExerciseWheelPicker.test.tsx 48/48 green, tsc clean. Capture = authenticated /activity screen (defect is behavioral, not a static frame).

judge.note: Exact root-cause match on both symptoms; distinct-coverage gate + replay guard confirmed in code; dedicated unit spec 48/48 green; tsc clean.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Live workout player declares a set the "final set" based purely on set NUMBER, not on whether all target sets were actually logged. In ExerciseWheelPicker.handleLogSet (src/components/ExerciseWheelPicker.tsx:341) it fires onSetComplete(true) whenever setData.set_number === targetSets, with no check that sets 1..targetSets-1 were logged. Activity.handleSetComplete (src/pages/Activity.tsx:672) then advances to the next exercise or declares the whole workout done. Two demonstrable symptoms from the same root cause:

(A) OUT-OF-ORDER LOG -> premature completion. Repro: open an exercise whose target is 3 sets (e.g. 3x8-10), tap the Set 3 row to activate it, and log it FIRST (reverse-pyramid / top-set-first is common for the strength persona this app targets). Expected: nothing special; sets 1-2 still pending. Actual: onSetComplete(true) fires -> if more exercises remain, the "Set complete - Next up" banner pops prompting the user to move on; if this is the last exercise, "Workout complete" + confetti + completion sound fire with only 1 of 3 sets logged.

(B) EDIT-AFTER-COMPLETE -> celebration replays. Repro: log all 3 sets of the LAST exercise normally (workout-complete banner shows, confetti + sound fire once - correct). The picker stays mounted/open above the banner. Tap the already-logged Set 3 row -> the editor expands -> tap "Update". Expected: a silent value update. Actual: handleLogSet runs again with set_number === targetSets -> onSetComplete(true) -> Activity.handleSetComplete else-branch unconditionally re-runs setShowWorkoutCelebration(true) + playCompleteCue(), so the confetti overlay and completion sound REPLAY on every edit of the final set.

Fix: gate completion on distinct logged target sets covering 1..target_sets (count reached), not on set_number equality; and skip re-firing the celebration when showWorkoutComplete is already true.

previousFix.description: Root cause: logSetMutation.onSuccess toasted 'Set logged' for EVERY set, so the quick-complete checkbox auto-log path (handleCheckboxToggle logs every prior-session set with the picker closed) stacked 4-5 toasts from a single tap, breaking the calm-design no-popups-on-routine-taps rule. Fix: the per-set onSuccess toast now fires only when the picker is actually open (isModalOpen.current, Activity.tsx:472) i.e. manual logging; the auto-log path keeps just its single '{exercise} auto-logged' summary toast. Verified: tsc clean, ExerciseWheelPicker.test.tsx 48/48 green. Capture = authenticated /activity screen (toast-stacking is behavioral, not a static frame).

judge.note: Per-set toast now gated on isModalOpen.current so auto-log emits one summary toast only; matches the described fix exactly; tsc clean.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Quick-complete checkbox auto-log spams one toast per set (4-5 stacked toasts from a single tap), breaking the calm-design "no popups on routine taps" rule. logSetMutation.onSuccess (src/pages/Activity.tsx:464-469) unconditionally shows a "Set logged. Set N: X reps x Ykg" toast for EVERY logged set. Activity.handleCheckboxToggle (src/pages/Activity.tsx:759-766) loops over the previous session's sets and calls logSetMutation.mutateAsync once per set, then fires an extra "{exercise} auto-logged" toast.

Repro: on /activity, find an exercise that has prior-session data (so the quick-complete checkbox is shown, not the manual "+" button), tap the checkbox once. Expected: a single confirmation toast. Actual: for a 4-set exercise the user gets 4x "Set logged..." toasts PLUS the "{exercise} auto-logged" toast = 5 stacked toasts from one tap.

Fix: suppress the per-set onSuccess toast on the auto-log path (e.g. thread a silent flag through the mutation variables, or only toast when the picker is actually open), keeping just the single "auto-logged" summary toast.

fix.description: Root cause: cancel soft-cancels (status='canceled') but intentionally keeps current_period_end in the future, yet both entitlement reads gated on status=='active' (entitlement.py:58 has_active_subscription + backend.py:2065 /auth/me subscription_active), so premium was revoked the instant Cancel was tapped - contradicting the 'keep access until <date>' promise. Fix: both reads now accept status in ('active','canceled'); get_active_subscription already excludes expired rows, so access ends exactly at current_period_end (cancel stops auto-renew, not access). Backend commit 02c7027, deployed + health-checked. Proof: prod E2E (rolled back) - canceled-in-period => access TRUE, canceled-expired => access FALSE.

judge.note: Owner-prescribed fix applied verbatim to both files; deployed to prod + health-green; verified end-to-end against the deployed code and real DB in a rolled-back transaction (in-period keeps access, expired loses it).

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description: [bug-hunt] Canceling a paid subscription revokes premium access IMMEDIATELY instead of at the end of the prepaid period - contradicting the cancel endpoint's own contract and the on-screen promise. ROOT CAUSE (backend): POST /api/v1/subscription/cancel (CancelSubscriptionResource, BACKEND backend.py:2861) soft-cancels by setting status='canceled' but INTENTIONALLY leaves current_period_end in the future so the user 'keeps access until the prepaid window ends' (its own docstring, backend.py:2812-2815). BUT both entitlement reads require status=='active': (1) entitlement.py:58 has_active_subscription() returns bool(sub and sub.status=='active') - this gates subscription_required, which 402s premium endpoints when FEATURE_SUBSCRIPTION_GATE is ON; (2) backend.py:2065 /auth/me sets subscription_active = bool(active_sub and active_sub.status=='active'). The comment two lines above (backend.py:2054-2055) literally says 'We include soft-canceled subs whose period hasn't elapsed because the FE treats period_end (not status) as the access boundary' - but the boolean then discards them via the status check, contradicting its own comment and get_active_subscription()'s documented 'may be soft-canceled but still within its period'. EXPECTED: after cancel, subscription_active stays true and premium stays unlocked until current_period_end; only auto-renew stops. ACTUAL: subscription_active flips false the instant Cancel is tapped. The FE cancel toast promises 'Your plan will remain active until the end of the current billing period' and SubscriptionSettings shows a 'You will keep access until <date>' banner, yet /auth/me already reports the user as unsubscribed; when the gate flips ON (documented rollout) the user is 402'd out of coach chat / AI builders immediately despite having paid through period_end. REPRO: paid/active user -> /choose-plan?manage=1 or /settings/subscription -> Cancel subscription -> confirm; the 'Current subscription' billing block + cancel affordance vanish instantly (both gate on user.subscription_active), and with the gate on premium endpoints return 402 on the next call. FIX: grant access to soft-canceled rows still within their period, e.g. status in ('active','canceled') with current_period_end>now, in BOTH BACKEND nyu_backend/app/services/entitlement.py:58 and nyu_backend/backend.py:2065.

previousFix.description: Root cause: SubscriptionSettings.handleRestore showed the 'Purchases restored' toast unconditionally in the try block; the backend returns HTTP 200 {restored:false} for a no-purchase account so axios never threw and the 'Nothing to restore' catch branch never ran. Fix: branch on res.data.restored (success toast only when restored===true, else the no-purchase message; catch still handles network/5xx), mirroring ChoosePlan. Proof: with the endpoint returning {restored:false} the screen now shows 'Nothing to restore / We couldn't find a previous purchase on this account.'

judge.note: Owner-prescribed fix applied verbatim; tsc clean; proven end-to-end in-browser with a {restored:false} response showing the correct 'Nothing to restore' toast.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description: [bug-hunt] Subscription screen shows a FALSE 'Purchases restored' success even when there is nothing to restore. FILE: src/pages/SubscriptionSettings.tsx handleRestore (~lines 177-197). The 'Restore previous purchase' button POSTs /payments/restore-purchases and UNCONDITIONALLY shows the success toast 'Purchases restored / Your subscription has been refreshed' in the try block - it never inspects the response. But the backend (RestoreSubscriptionResource, BACKEND backend.py:2955-2959) returns HTTP 200 with {restored:false, reason:'no active subscription found'} when there is no valid subscription. Because it is a 200 (not 4xx), axios does NOT throw, so the code never reaches the 'Nothing to restore' catch branch - that branch only fires on real network/5xx errors. EXPECTED: a user with no prior purchase taps Restore -> 'Nothing to restore / We couldn't find a previous purchase on this account'. ACTUAL: they get 'Purchases restored / Your subscription has been refreshed' (false success), then load() re-fetches and the card still shows status 'none' - the toast contradicts the screen. REPRO: log in as a free/never-paid account -> /settings/subscription -> tap 'Restore previous purchase' -> false success toast. FIX: read response.data.restored from the POST and branch on it (success toast only when restored===true; otherwise the no-purchases message), mirroring ChoosePlan.handleRestorePurchases which already gates its success toast on the response payload. Keep the catch branch for genuine network/5xx errors.

fix.description: Root cause: extractInlineOptions matched ANY parenthetical containing '/' and split on it, so unit expressions like '(3-4 km/day)', '(1.6 g/kg)', '(~300 kcal/serving)' became garbage answer chips (and, by producing a buttons element, suppressed the free-text fallback). Fix: reject segments that contain a digit or a bare unit token (day/kg/min/g/km/kcal/serving/...); real lists like '(strength / hypertrophy / fat loss)' still parse. Fixed both copies (AIWizardShell.tsx + AIMealCustomization.tsx). Proof: 6 new regression tests, 43/43 green (logic-only, LLM-output-dependent state not deterministically browser-reproducible).

judge.note: Exact repro strings from the issue now handled correctly; real option lists still parse; both duplicate copies fixed; locked by regression tests.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description: [bug-hunt] AI plan wizards turn unit parentheticals into garbage answer buttons. extractInlineOptions (src/components/ai/AIWizardShell.tsx:181, and the duplicate in src/pages/AIMealCustomization.tsx:22) matches ANY parenthetical containing '/' via /(([^)]*/[^)]*))/ and splits on '/', so unit expressions like '(3-4 km/day)', '(15-30 min/day)', '(1.6 g/kg)', '(~300 kcal/serving)' get parsed as an option list. Expected: only real slash-separated option lists such as '(strength / hypertrophy / fat loss)' become tappable buttons; unit expressions are ignored and the normal free-text input is shown. Actual (unit-tested): extractInlineOptions('Your target is ~8000 steps (roughly 3-4 km/day). Does that work?') => ['roughly 3-4 km','day'] — two nonsense buttons render. Tapping one sends that fragment (e.g. 'day') to the coach as the user's answer, corrupting the session; and because a buttons element is produced, elementRenderable becomes true, which SUPPRESSES the free-text fallback in AIWizardShell (only the small 'type instead' composer under a divider remains). LIVE on: /ai/create-activity-plan (the Activity wizard, which routinely says 'steps/day', 'km/day', 'min/day') and /ai/customize-meal (coach says 'kcal/serving', 'g/portion'). NOTE: AIDietPlanCreation.tsx is an orphaned copy — the live diet route /ai/create-diet-plan uses CustomDietPlanCreation.tsx. Repro: open the Activity plan wizard, let the coach ask a step-target/time question phrased with a '(x/unit)' parenthetical (or force a message like the test string) — nonsense chips appear instead of a usable input. Fix: only treat the parenthetical as options when it looks like a real list (>=2 slashes, i.e. 3+ segments; or reject when a trailing segment is a bare unit token like day/kg/min/g/km/mi/hr/serving/portion; or require each segment to be a short word-like phrase). Fix both copies (AIWizardShell + AIMealCustomization).

fix.description: Root cause: isConfirmationPrompt used includes('ready') — which matches the substring inside 'already' — plus broad phrases ('here's your'/'personalized'/'set up') gated only by ANY of plan|program|daily|repeat, so normal mid-flow questions ('plan isn''t ready yet…daily', 'already on a plan…daily?') were misclassified as confirmations and rendered premature Confirm/Make-Changes buttons. Fix (AIWizardShell.tsx): guard negated readiness ('isn''t/not…ready'), match whole-word \bready\b, and require an explicit confirm/finished-plan cue (confirm / look good / all set / 'plan is ready') before the confirm buttons render. Genuine 'plan is ready! Confirm' still triggers them. Proof: 6 new regression tests, 43/43 green (logic-only, LLM-output-dependent state not deterministically browser-reproducible).

judge.note: Both reported false-positive strings now return false; genuine confirmation + button payloads still work; locked by regression tests.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description: [bug-hunt] isConfirmationPrompt over-matches, showing a premature 'Confirm Plan / Make Changes' pair mid-flow. In src/components/ai/AIWizardShell.tsx:315-321 the check uses lower.includes('ready') — which also matches the substring inside 'already' — plus other broad phrases ('here's your', 'personalized', 'set up'), gated only by ANY of 'plan'|'program'|'daily'|'repeat'. Expected: the Confirm/Make-Changes buttons appear only when the coach is actually presenting a finished plan for confirmation. Actual (unit-tested): isConfirmationPrompt("Your plan isn't ready yet — I'm still calculating your daily targets.") => true; isConfirmationPrompt("You're already on a plan — want to rebuild it daily?") => true. When the backend omits a ui_element (common — the entire extractInlineOptions/generateFallbackOptions/isConfirmationPrompt fallback layer exists because the LLM frequently forgets the ui block), a normal mid-flow QUESTION containing 'already'/'here's your' + 'daily'/'plan' is misclassified as a confirmation, so the wizard renders 'Confirm Plan' and 'Make Changes' buttons in the middle of the intake. Tapping them sends the canned strings 'Yes, confirm' / 'I want to make changes' instead of an answer to the real question, derailing the session. LIVE on /ai/create-activity-plan (uses AIWizardShell). Repro: in the Activity wizard, when the coach asks a clarifying question phrased with 'here's your daily …' or containing 'already' + a plan word and sends no ui_element, the confirm buttons appear prematurely. Fix: match whole word 'ready' with a boundary ( ready ) and tighten the phrase set / require a stronger confirmation signal (e.g. combine with a plan-preview or an explicit 'confirm'/'look good' cue) before rendering the confirm buttons.

fix.description: Fixed: move reconnect_attempt from socket to socket.io (Manager). socket.io-client v4 emits Manager lifecycle events only on Manager, not Socket. Old handler was dead code; now socket.io.on fires on each retry. Token refresh runs before reconnect attempts. TS clean, tests pass.

judge.note: One-line fix in correct location; root cause (Manager vs Socket emitter) verified against socket.io-client source. TS noEmit clean, unit tests pass.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description: [bug-hunt] Socket auto-reconnect always retries with the STALE token captured at connect time - the pre-reconnect token-refresh hook is dead code listening on the wrong emitter. chat.service.ts:168 registers `this.socket.on('reconnect_attempt', ...)` (refreshes the access token and swaps socket.auth + query.token before each retry), but in socket.io-client v4 (repo ships 4.8.3) reconnect lifecycle events are emitted ONLY on the Manager - `socket.io.on('reconnect_attempt')`; the Socket instance never receives them (verified: node_modules/socket.io-client/build/cjs/manager.js:379 is the sole emitter, socket.js re-emits nothing). Expected: each reconnect attempt carries a freshly-rotated token, as the code comment states. Actual: after any network blip the manager retries with the ORIGINAL token from the connect() closure; if the token was refreshed/expired/revoked meanwhile, the backend connect handler rejects every attempt ('Authentication failed.' + disconnect, backend.py:14382), all 10 reconnectionAttempts burn, and the app-wide singleton socket stays dead for the session (chat deltas, image_ready, streak_update, partner events) until an app-foreground or chat-page mount calls connect() again. Repro (static + empirical): attach both listeners and drop the network - the Manager listener fires per attempt, the Socket listener never does. Fix: one line - register the handler on this.socket.io instead of this.socket. File: src/services/chat.service.ts:165-180.

fix.description: Fixed two bugs: (1) disconnect() now fires disconnectCallbacks BEFORE removing the 'disconnect' handler so useChatSocket.isSocketConnected flips false and polling fallback engages; (2) handleSocketError auth-recovery path snapshots newMessageCallback/errorCallback/aiTypingCallback before disconnect() and restores them after connect() so the open chat screen keeps receiving messages without a page remount. TS clean, tests pass.

judge.note: Both bugs fixed at described code lines. Callbacks snapshot+restore is the correct pattern; polling fallback now engages on teardown. TS noEmit clean.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description: [bug-hunt] After the socket's 'Authentication failed.' recovery reconnect, an OPEN coach-chat screen goes permanently deaf: incoming AI replies never render (while the unread badge lights up), the typing indicator freezes, and the polling fallback never engages. Chain: handleSocketError (chat.service.ts:361) on 'Authentication failed.' refreshes the token, then calls this.disconnect() + this.connect(userId). disconnect() (1) nulls the single-slot callbacks newMessageCallback / aiTypingCallback / errorCallback (chat.service.ts:256-258), which are only registered by useChatSocket's mount effect - a service-internal reconnect re-runs no React effect, so they stay null; and (2) detaches the socket 'disconnect' handler BEFORE calling socket.disconnect() (line 242 vs 254), so disconnectCallbacks never fire, useChatSocket's isSocketConnected stays true, and CoachChat's 60s polling fallback (CoachChat.tsx:104-108) never turns on. Net effect: new_message events still reach handleNewMessage, which sets nyus_has_unread_coach - the user sits INSIDE the chat watching an unread badge appear while no bubble renders, until they leave and re-enter the page. Ironically the comment at chat.service.ts:259-265 preserves the connect/disconnect REGISTRIES for exactly this code path but misses the single-slot callbacks two lines above it. Trigger is real: access-token rotation/expiry mid-session or a token_version bump (owner login) makes the backend reject the socket handshake with 'Authentication failed.'; the refresh then succeeds and the recovery path runs. Expected: after the internal recovery reconnect, the open chat keeps receiving messages (or at minimum the polling fallback engages). Fix: snapshot + restore the callback slots across the auth-recovery reconnect (or convert them to multi-subscriber registries like connectCallbacks), and invoke disconnectCallbacks on teardown. issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description: [bug-hunt] Language choice from the startup picker is DESTROYED on every app restart - app always reverts to English. Root cause: main.tsx calls initI18n() with no arg, and config.ts defaults lng=DEFAULT_LOCALE(en), passing an explicit lng:'en' to i18next.init(). Per i18next semantics, an explicit lng bypasses LanguageDetector entirely (stored nyus_locale is never read), AND because detection.caches=['localStorage'], the boot-time changeLanguage('en') REWRITES nyus_locale back to 'en', permanently erasing the user's Hindi/Hinglish choice. Reproduced empirically with the repo's i18next 23.16.8: localStorage nyus_locale='hi' + init with lng:'en' -> language=en and nyus_locale overwritten to 'en'; same init WITHOUT lng -> language=hi, storage intact. Expected: pick Hindi once, app stays Hindi forever. Actual: Hindi only until next launch; picker never re-shows (nyus_lang_picker_shown), so user is stuck in English. Fix: drop the lng option from init (let detector resolve), or pass getStoredLocale() ?? undefined. Files: src/main.tsx:21, src/i18n/config.ts:66-76 (lng param + supportedLngs), src/pages/LanguagePicker.tsx:11-14. Introduced 5f79d6b2 (i18n P1).

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Startup language picker promises the coach speaks your language but never sets coach_language - Hindi/Hinglish pickers still get an ENGLISH AI coach. The picker subtitle literally says 'apni bhasha mein baat karein' (talk in your language), yet setAppLocale() (src/pages/LanguagePicker.tsx:11) only calls i18n.changeLanguage + writes nyus_locale. The backend coach_language pref (drives AI reply language, shipped for i-20260707-lng1) is only settable from Profile > Preferences (ProfilePreferencesCard.tsx handleLangChange -> PUT /profile). Nothing bridges the two: grep shows nyus_locale is read nowhere except the i18n detector, and coach_language is written nowhere except the profile card. Expected: pick Hindi at startup -> UI AND coach replies in Hindi. Actual: coach replies in English until the user separately discovers the buried Profile toggle. Repro: fresh install -> pick Hindi -> onboard -> open coach chat -> replies are English; GET /profile shows coach_language english. Fix: picker is pre-auth, so stash the choice (e.g. from nyus_locale) and apply it to coach_language at login/onboarding finalize (map hi->hindi, hinglish->hinglish, en->english).
